captions.instagram:
How does the excretory system work?

Every day you get rid of about 1 kg of carbon dioxide, a litre and a half of urine and a surprising amount of sweat. See all four ways out in a see-through body, watch the liver lock toxic ammonia into urea, fill a bladder until the brain says go, and swap sweat for urine on a hot day.

→ Your body gets rid of waste four ways: urine, breath, sweat and stool.
→ The kidneys make urine, and the lungs, liver, gut and skin share the rest of the work.
→ Every day you breathe out about 1 kg of carbon dioxide, your biggest waste by far.
→ Urea goes out in urine, and old red blood cells leave as bile pigment in stool.
→ Protein leaves toxic ammonia behind, and the liver locks it safely into urea.

youtubeLong.description:
Every day you get rid of about 1 kg of carbon dioxide, a litre and a half of urine and a surprising amount of sweat. See all four ways out in a see-through body, watch the liver lock toxic ammonia into urea, fill a bladder until the brain says go, and swap sweat for urine on a hot day.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/excretionclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/excretionclear

In this video:
• Four ways out. The body gets rid of waste four ways: urine from the kidneys, carbon dioxide from the lungs, sweat from the skin and stool carrying bile from the liver.
• What you throw away every day. About 1 kg of carbon dioxide, 20–35 g of urea, about 0.3 g of bilirubin from old red blood cells, and about 2.5 litres of water split between urine, skin, breath and stool.
• Turning poison into urea. Protein leaves nitrogen behind as toxic ammonia.
• Hold on. The bladder stretches while pressure stays low.
• Sweat or urine. Heat and exercise send water out as sweat, so ADH rises and urine turns small and dark.
• Keeping it healthy. About half of women get a bladder infection at some point.
